title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ（斉藤博嗣研究室）
subtitle: Design Project III(Saito Hiroshi)
teachers:
SAITO Hiroshi
授業科目の学習・教育目標
educationalGoal:
(1) Acquire the ability to identify and solve problems to research, develop, design, and manufacture socially useful and high-quality products using the basic knowledge learned in the Department of Mechanical Engineering.
(2) Learn what technologies or new mechanisms are needed for that purpose.
(3) Learn about the importance of collaboration with society (particularly local communities).
advice:
This is the final comprehensive course in the Department of Mechanical Engineering. To realize the educational objectives of the Department of Mechanical Engineering, this course focuses on the following goals:
  Students will acquire the ability to model phenomena accurately and analyze the models.
  Students will acquire the ability and the engineering sense to evaluate solutions based on the obtained results.
In practice, students should reconfirm their project theme, which was determined in Preparatory Seminar, with the supervisors of the individual laboratories. (The theme should be revised as necessary.)
Students are expected to pursue the identification and solution of problems in accordance with the engineering process.
This laboratory focuses on the composite materials widely applied in aerospace equipment, ships, vehicles, energy equipment, construction materials, and sporting goods. Students practically learn the impact of many factors on manufacturing, designing and failure mechanisms through manufacturing, testing and analysis composite materials by themselves. Also, students work on specific technical issues through collaboration with local communities in some parts of these activities. We aim to cultivate flexible and comprehensive thinking abilities regardless of the academic field. Discussions and presentations can be performed using online tools as needed.

requiredKnowledge: Broad fundamental knowledge from fields such as mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology, dynamics, materials, technical drawing, and finite element analysis is necessary to develop material evaluation, design, and molding methods based on the clarification of the fracture mechanisms in composite materials. Be able to compile the results correctly into an article and discuss the content through presentations.
Be able to act independently to solve the issues presented separately.

achievementLevels.ideal:
(1) Understand the purpose of the project theme and process accurately, and achieve the established annual goal. The process can be reported in some ways.
(2) Compile the intermediate results for the project into the interim report, and present and discuss its content. Complete the final report, present it, and discuss its content. The final results can be published in journals of academic societies for each specialized field.
(3) If necessary, design and manufacture the own experimental devices, and also evaluate the performance of the product.
achievementLevels.standard:
(1) Understand the purpose of your project theme and the advancement process, and achieve the established annual goal. In addition, the process can be reported in some ways.
(2) Compile intermediate results for the project into the interim report, and present its content. Complete the final report and present it.
(3) Design and manufacture your own experimental devices if necessary.

              This is the final comprehensive course in the Department of Mechanical Engineering. To realize the educational objectives of the Department of Mechanical Engineering, this course focuses on the following goals:
  Students will acquire the ability to model phenomena accurately and analyze the models.
  Students will acquire the ability and the engineering sense to evaluate solutions based on the obtained results.
In practice, students should reconfirm their project theme, which was determined in Preparatory Seminar, with the supervisors of the individual laboratories. (The theme should be revised as necessary.)
Students are expected to pursue the identification and solution of problems in accordance with the engineering process.
This laboratory focuses on the composite materials widely applied in aerospace equipment, ships, vehicles, energy equipment, construction materials, and sporting goods. Students practically learn the impact of many factors on manufacturing, designing and failure mechanisms through manufacturing, testing and analysis composite materials by themselves. Also, students work on specific technical issues through collaboration with local communities in some parts of these activities. We aim to cultivate flexible and comprehensive thinking abilities regardless of the academic field. Discussions and presentations can be performed using online tools as needed.
